**civicbeam** — six stores hold personal data:

| Store | Kind | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `users` | relational | no_entry_point |
| `documents` | relational | no_entry_point |
| `uploads` (S3, `docs/{user_id}/…`) | object storage | no_entry_point |
| `doc_search` | search index | no_entry_point |
| `events` | queue | no_entry_point |
| `nightly_dump` | backup | no_schedule_evidenced |

The repository has no account-deletion path at all: `api/account.py` defines only `create_document` and `get_profile`, and a grep for delete/remove/purge across the tree returns one line — the `cascade="all, delete"` on `User.documents` (`models.py:19`), which never fires because nothing deletes a `User`. That is why every store carries `no_entry_point` rather than `not_erased`.

The dump job writes `email`, `full_name` and `phone` to a JSON file (`jobs/dump.py:9`) with no cron entry, timer or retention constant anywhere in the code, so the retention table is empty — no number was invented.

Observations recorded, not findings: region `eu-central-1` (`config.py:9`), Elasticsearch and RabbitMQ hosts (`config.py:10-11`), and S3 `ServerSideEncryption="AES256"` (`storage.py:21`) as an Art. 32(1)(a) measure. `catalog.py` (Plan) and `utils/text.py` are outside the record — no link to a person. `README.md` and `requirements.txt` are listed as unscanned, not Python.
